purpose: Explicit ground-plane declarations for templates that model an excavation.
rationale: structure_geometry_lint.check_structural_connectivity anchors its flood fill on the
template's own lowest solid layer. That is correct for a building, whose lowest course
is its footing, and wrong for a template that models a pit: there the lowest solid layer
is the excavated floor, tens of blocks below the grade the site's haul road, yard
buildings and plant actually stand on, so every at-grade structure is reported floating.
A declaration here does NOT excuse a site from having ground. The declared level must be
a real, built ground course in the template - if a structure hovers above the declared
plane it is reported exactly as before. The declaration only tells the gate which plane
counts as grade; it is not a suppression list, and it must never be used as one.
Keys are the structure path relative to the scanned directory, without the .nbt suffix,
matching the structure_id the standalone linter prints.

ows_012_atlas_bulk_crushing_preparation_.reason: Open-pit quarry. Pit floor sits at y=2 and the benches carry it up to the rim; the haul road bed, service house, crushing plant and headframe all stand on the working yard at y=12, which is built as an industrial-hardstanding grade course by _authored_012 in scripts/generate_old_world_narrative_structures.py.
